sources.outlet: Journal of Substance Abuse Treatment (Harris, Abraham, Lozano-Rojas, Negaro, Andrews, Grogan)
sources.quote: About half of states received less than $100.00 dollars per capita in the state corrections population.
sources.searcher_note: Closest pattern: FY2019 federal opioid money for the criminal-legal system (10 agencies, 517 grants, $590M) was unevenly spread relative to need; says ~34.2% would need reallocating. State level, not county; not the same flagged-county set.

sources.quote: When counties spend money on jails, they have less money to spend on substance use treatment, harm reduction services, and other community-based resources that could prevent overdoses and improve community health and wellness.
sources.searcher_note: Links county jail incarceration and overdose death rates (the 'double burden' idea); argues jail spending crowds out treatment. Does not measure SAMHSA dollars per person in those counties.

sources.quote: SAMHSA allocates funding based on factors such as overdose death rates, and recently revised its allocation to better ensure funding goes to recipients with the greatest need.
sources.searcher_note: Leans the other way: GAO says State Opioid Response money is allocated on overdose death rates (state level, $8.1B since FY2018). Does not address county-level distribution or jail rates.

sources.quote: Federal Opioid Grant Funding Favors Least Populous States, Not States With Greatest Need
sources.searcher_note: Headline only; page returned 403 to fetch. State-level pattern: federal opioid grants not tracking need. Not county level.

notes: No source found that measures SAMHSA dollars per person in counties flagged for both high overdose and high jail incarceration, or any county-level comparison close to $45 vs $92. Coverage found is state-level (Harris 2023, Health Affairs, GAO) or conceptual (Vera on jail spending vs treatment). GAO leans the other way at state level: SOR allocation is based on overdose death rates. A Columbia Journal of Global Health piece on 2021 SAMHSA allocation (search snippet: states with more deaths got more, but high-rate states underfunded per population) was blocked on fetch, not recorded. Bipartisan Policy Center county-level funding maps (2015-17, five states) returned 403, not recorded. Jan 2026 SAMHSA grant cut-and-restore coverage (WaPo, NPR) is not about county allocation.
